$$
{A}^{T}\,A=[\begin{aligned}68 & 26 \\ 26 & 29\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}{v}_{11} & {v}_{12} \\ {v}_{21} & {v}_{22}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the value of $|{v}_{12}|+|{v}_{22}|?$
questions.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ the columns of $V$ must be the right singular vectors of $A,$ i.e., the unit eigenvectors of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=9$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=4.$ So, the second column of $V$ corresponds to the singular value ${\sigma }_{2}=4.$

Hence, we need to find a unit eigenvector of ${A}^{T}\,A$ that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=16.$ Computing ${A}^{T}\,A-16I,$ we get

$$
{A}^{T}\,A-16I=[\begin{aligned}68 & 26 \\ 26 & 29\end{aligned}]-16[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}52 & 26 \\ 26 & 13\end{aligned}]
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-16I)v=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we get 

$$
\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
|{v}_{12}|+|{v}_{22}|=|-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}|+|\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}|=\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=4$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=1.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=16,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-16I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 13\end{aligned}]-16[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-12 & -6 \\ -6 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-16I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 13\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -6 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{8}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ the columns of $V$ must be the right singular vectors of $A,$ i.e., the unit eigenvectors of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$

Hence, we need to find a unit eigenvector of ${A}^{T}\,A$ that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=81.$ Computing ${A}^{T}\,A-81I,$ we get

$$
{A}^{T}\,A-81I=[\begin{aligned}73 & 24 \\ 24 & 9\end{aligned}]-81[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 24 \\ 24 & -72\end{aligned}]

$$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A,$ $Σ,$ and $V$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the second column of $U?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ and ${\sigma }_{i}\ne 0,$ then the $i$th column of $U$ can be found as

$$
{u}_{i}=\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{i}}A{v}_{i},
$$

 

where ${v}_{i}$ is the $i$th column of the matrix $V.$

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=6$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=4.$ Therefore, the second column of $U$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{12}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}65 & 4 \\ 4 & 80\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=9$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=8.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=81,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-81I & =[\begin{aligned}65 & 4 \\ 4 & 80\end{aligned}]-81[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-16 & 4 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-81I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=64,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-64I & =[\begin{aligned}65 & 4 \\ 4 & 80\end{aligned}]-64[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 4 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-64I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{9}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{36}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{32}{\sqrt{17}} \\ -\frac{8}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} & -\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}} & -\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{17}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}]
$$
